title: Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches, And all phenomena — Desirable, delightful, agreeable — Thus they are called. Devas and humans in the world, Regarding them…
content:
Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches,
And all phenomena —
Desirable, delightful, agreeable —
Thus they are called.

Devas and humans in the world,
Regarding them as delightful —
Where they cease and fade away,
Devas and humans see suffering.

The noble one sees as ease
When identity view is destroyed —
The noble one sees as opposite
All the views of the world.

What others call pleasure,
The noble call suffering.
What others call suffering,
The noble know as pleasure.

See the Dhamma, hard to comprehend,
Where the ignorant are bewildered —
Darkness for the blind,
Obscurity for those who cannot see.

For the good person with open eyes,
Light is clearly seen —
Living close, they know clearly,
Skilled in the great Dhamma.

Overcome by the thirst of birth,
Swept away by the current of existence,
Subject to Māra’s control —
They do not awaken to this Dhamma.

Apart from the noble ones, no one
Awakens to this path —
The path leading to Nibbāna,
With perfect wisdom, free from defilements.

title: “But this body, Aggivessana, is material, composed of the four great elements, born of father and mother, nourished with rice and porridge, impermanent, subject to…
content: “But this body, Aggivessana, is material, composed of the four great elements, born of father and mother, nourished with rice and porridge, impermanent, subject to rubbing, pressing, breaking, disintegration, dissolution. It should be contemplated as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. When he contemplates this body as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease … as not-self, then bodily desire, bodily fondness, bodily subjection are abandoned.”

title: Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a…
content:
Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a udumbara staff, approached those monks. Having approached, he said to them:
- “Venerable sirs, you have gone forth too young, in the prime of youth, with black hair, in the bloom of youth, at the early stage of life, without having enjoyed sensual pleasures. Venerable sirs, enjoy human sensual pleasures. Do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time.”

- “Brahmin, we do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time. And, brahmin, we abandon what is subject to time to chase after the present. The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are subject to time, of great suffering, of great despair — the peril in them is even greater. This Dhamma is visible here and now, not subject to time, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: The inner fetter and the outer fetter — Beings are entangled in these fetters. I ask Gotama about this — Who can escape these fetters?…
content:
The inner fetter and the outer fetter —
Beings are entangled in these fetters.
I ask Gotama about this —
Who can escape these fetters?

(The Blessed One)
A person established in virtue, wise,
Developing mind and wisdom,
Ardent and discreet —
That monk can escape the fetters.
One who has abandoned greed,
Hatred, and ignorance,
The defilement-free arahant —
He has escaped the fetters.
Where name-and-form is destroyed
Without remainder,
Where the hindrance and perceptions of form are destroyed —
There the fetters are cut.

title: - “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?” - “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for…
content:
- “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
- “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings.”
- “But how, venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
The destruction of delight in renewed existence,
The cessation of perception and consciousness,
The stilling of feelings —
Thus, friend, I know the release,
The escape and seclusion
For all kinds of beings.

title: “Monks, having heard Brahmā’s request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, I saw beings with little…
content: “Monks, having heard Brahmā’s request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and with dull faculties, with good dispositions and with bad dispositions, some easy to teach and some hard to teach, and a few who saw the danger in rebirth to another world and the danger of faulty actions. Just as in a blue lotus pond, a red lotus pond, or a white lotus pond, some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, and do not rise above the water, being nourished underwater; some are born in the water, grow in the water, and reach the water’s surface; some are born in the water, grow in the water, and rise up above the water, not wetted by the water.”

title: All conditioned things are truly impermanent, They arise and then pass away — Their nature is always thus. They come into being, Then they again…
content:
All conditioned things are truly impermanent,
They arise and then pass away —
Their nature is always thus.
They come into being,
Then they again are destroyed.
Blissful indeed when they
Are calmed and at peace.

title: “And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled…
content: “And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. Thus, monks, is non-restraint.”

title: Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One: How does a monk, Living amidst many obstacles, Having crossed the five…
content:
Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One:
How does a monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strive to cross the sixth?
How can he meditate,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
So that they remain outside him,
Not catching him?

(The Blessed One):
With body tranquilized,
With mind well liberated,
With no more activities,
Mindful, without clinging,
Knowing the Dhamma,
Without thought, meditating —
Without anger, without distraction,
Without drowsiness, without laziness —
Thus the monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strives to cross the sixth.
Thus he meditates,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
They remain outside him,
Not catching him.

title: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the…
content: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, consumed by sensual thoughts, and strives for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a fool, not an elder. But if a young person, brahmin, a youth with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, does not enjoy sensual pleasures, does not dwell amidst sensual pleasures, is not burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, not consumed by sensual thoughts, and does not strive for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a wise one, an elder.”
